stem_book: A square frame is made of four uniform rods, the mass of each rod being m and its length l. Match the axis of rotation in Column-I with the moment of inertia about it in Column-II. Column-I: (A) axis in the plane of the frame through one corner, parallel to a diagonal (frame held as a diamond, horizontal axis through the top vertex); (B) axis along one side of the frame; (C) axis along a diagonal; (D) axis perpendicular to the plane of the frame through the mid-point of one side. Column-II: (P) (2/3)ml² (Q) (5/3)ml² (R) (7/3)ml² (S) (8/3)ml². (a) (A)-(S), (B)-(Q), (C)-(P), (D)-(R) (b) (A)-(P), (B)-(Q), (C)-(R), (D)-(S) (c) (A)-(S), (B)-(P), (C)-(Q), (D)-(R) (d) (A)-(R), (B)-(S), (C)-(P), (D)-(Q)
reason: Column-I axes exist only as drawings; described them in words
work: I_⊥centre = 4[ml²/12 + ml²/4] = 4ml²/3, in-plane centre axis = 2ml²/3 (C, P); side: 2/3 + 4m(l/2)² ⇒ 5/3 (Q); corner ∥ diagonal: 2/3 + 4m(l²/2) ⇒ 8/3 (S); ⊥ at side mid-point: 4/3 + 1 = 7/3 (R)
